react_result.final_narrative_text: The differentially abundant metabolites map onto a single dominant biological axis: arachidonic acid metabolism and its downstream eicosanoid products. Cross-paradigm consensus across mummichog (empirical-compound network, rank 0, p=0.0041), RaMP multi-DB ORA (WikiPathways, FDR=3.2×10⁻¹³), and MetaboAnalystR PSEA (KEGG, top hit) confirms that the arachidonic acid / eicosanoid cascade is the primary affected pathway. Five structurally confirmed driver metabolites (arachidonic acid, 5-HETE, 15-HETE, leukotriene A4, and 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ2) share the same InChIKey first-block across all three tools, ruling out any namespace artefact. Arachidonic acid (CHEBI:15843) is the upstream substrate for both the lipoxygenase branch (5-LOX → 5-HETE and 15-LOX → 15-HETE) and the cyclooxygenase branch (COX-1/2 → PGD2 → 15d-PGJ2), as well as the entry point for leukotriene A4 synthesis via 5-LOX. 15d-PGJ2 (KEGG:C14717) is the strongest contextual signal: it is a canonical PPARγ agonist and electrophilic cyclopentenone prostaglandin whose elevation implicates oxidative-stress-responsive Nrf2 activation. Acetylcysteine (KEGG:C06809) is the glutathione precursor and electrophilic scavenger; its differential abundance is consistent with a compensatory anti-oxidative response co-occurring with elevated cyclopentenone prostaglandins. Fructose 1-phosphate (KEGG:C01094) and dopamine (KEGG:C03758) did not achieve significance in the ORA paradigms and appear peripheral to the eicosanoid axis. The convergence of five lipid mediators across three independent analytical paradigms points to a treatment-induced perturbation of membrane phospholipid remodeling and eicosanoid biosynthesis, consistent with inflammation or a COX/LOX-inhibiting intervention.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent analytical paradigms converge on a single dominant pathway in this differential metabolome. RaMP multi-database ORA identifies Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) as the top hit with an FDR of 3.16×10⁻¹³ and five overlapping metabolites: 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-prostaglandin J₂, arachidonic acid, 5(S)-HETE, 15(S)-HETE, and leukotriene A₄. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently returns hsa00590 as the top result, also implicating arachidonic acid, 5-HETE, 15-HETE, and leukotriene A₄. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis confirms arachidonic acid metabolism as the highest-ranked network (p=0.0034) and additionally detects Glycerophospholipid metabolism (p=0.0095) and Leukotriene metabolism (p=0.0417). Across all three tools the shared driver compounds are arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219), 5-HETE (KEGG:C04805), 15-HETE (KEGG:C04742), and leukotriene A₄ (KEGG:C00909). 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ₂ (KEGG:C14717) anchors the COX/PGD₂ branch. Acetylcysteine, fructose 1-phosphate, and dopamine do not contribute to the eicosanoid axis and appear as non-significant outliers in all paradigms.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent analytical paradigms converge on arachidonic acid cascade pathways in this differential metabolome. RaMP multi-database ORA identifies Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) as its top hit, with 5 of 8 input metabolites mapping to the pathway (15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-prostaglandin J₂, arachidonic acid, 5-HETE, 15-HETE, and leukotriene A4) at FDR 3.16×10⁻¹³. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis detects Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism) as its highest-ranked network (p=0.00420) and Glycerophospholipid metabolism (MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism) at rank 2 (p=0.0117); both include multiple HETE species and arachidonic acid as overlapping compounds. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA returns hsa00590 at rank 1 with four metabolites (arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15-HETE, 5-HETE) providing KEGG-namespace corroboration. Leukotriene metabolism (MUMM:leukotriene_metabolism) appears as a fourth hit in Mummichog at p=0.0397. The five eicosanoid-axis compounds (15-deoxy-PGJ₂, arachidonic acid, 5-HETE, 15-HETE, leukotriene A4) are verified members of WP:WP167 by RaMP, and arachidonic acid participates as substrate via COX/LOX enzymes (PTGS1/ALOX5) that generate the downstream HETEs and leukotrienes. Fructose 1-phosphate and dopamine are absent from the eicosanoid cluster and appear only in carbohydrate/glycolysis pathway hits.
